method: Keep-alive HTTP; median of three interleaved passes; every response checked. Cross-runtime comparison: four client processes, sixteen connections each. One kiln realm; other runtimes may use multiple threads.

workloads.label: Hello world
workloads.description: A hello-world HTTP response, with no request body.
workloads.takeaway: kiln leads this hello-world workload. This result does not extend to every kind of request.

workloads.label: Small service
workloads.description: URL routing, query parsing, JSON, POST bodies, an 8 KB response, header echo and an async timer.
workloads.takeaway: Bun, Node and Deno are faster here. Request-body delivery through generic compiled Readable code is a current bottleneck.

workloads.label: 1 KB JSON echo
workloads.description: An HTTP JSON echo workload with a 1 KB body.
workloads.takeaway: Deno and Bun lead this body-heavy workload. kiln’s lower memory use does not imply higher throughput.

scaling.method: Same machine and date; ten client processes to load several workers. These are a separate run from the four-client cross-runtime comparison. The load generator shares the server’s cores.

takeaways.service: The small service reaches 60.3k requests/s with auto (16) workers: about 3× the one-worker result in this run.
takeaways.hello: Hello world peaks at four workers in this run. More workers are not always faster: the load generator shares the same cores.
